text:
ria_support: Customer (Acme) reporting sudden 429s during an ingest spike. They say total token usage for the project is low but bursts from a proxyed pool blow past limits and we return 429s.

mike_sre: Can you paste the exact error payload and a short repro curl? Also are they using an API key per-project or a single org key?

ria_support: Error snippet from their logs: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "rate_limited", "scope": "unknown" }` They say requests come from an autoscaler that NATs through 3 public IPs. Auth is via Authorization: Bearer <api_key> header. We created the API key under the org root (not project-scoped).

anya_billing: Quick check on our side: the org key has a monthly commit but no per-project quota; the project in question has an explicit low request cap set by the customer in the UI (sync rules). That could cause project-level throttles if the request is attributed to the project.

mike_sre: Important nuance: our limiter evaluates quota provenance at auth time. If a request comes with a valid API key we should attribute to the key -> project -> org chain. But if the proxy strips auth or re-writes headers we can end up attributing to source IP which falls into different buckets (IP-based limits are much lower). Can you confirm headers we see on the requests from their proxy?

ria_support: They sent a capture:

```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-inference.test
Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-org-xxx
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5
X-Real-IP: 35.199.12.7
User-Agent: AcmeIngest/1.2
```

They said their proxy terminates TLS and forwards using our public IPs; X-Forwarded-For contains internal IPs.

mike_sre: That explains it. If X-Forwarded-For is an internal address (10.x) we ignore it for source IP provenance; we then use the connection-level IP (35.199.12.7) which is one of their NAT egress IPs. Because many instances share that set of egress IPs, per-IP burst buckets are exhausted quickly.

derek_prod: Quick repro I used from our side: 50 concurrent short requests with that org key + NATed IP -> majority succeed, then we hit 429s within 20s. Headers I used:

```
curl -s -D- -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-org-xxx" \
  -H "User-Agent: AcmeIngest/1.2" \
  -d '{"input": "hi"}' &
# run in a loop 100x from same egress IP
```

mike_sre: Two actionable items: 1) short term workaround: advise customer to create a project-scoped API key (so quota attribution is locked to that project and avoids falling back to IP buckets) or use our dedicated egress for large customers. 2) long term: we should improve provenance logging when we decide which quota bucket to charge (API-key vs project vs IP) so support can see exactly why a request was charged to a given bucket.

anya_billing: Customer asked whether we can raise their project cap temporarily. I can patch a temporary bump if support adds the audit note and customer agrees to a one-time overage.

ria_support: I added the audit note and recommended the project-scoped key first. Customer accepted the temporary bump while they rotate keys.

mike_sre: Filing a follow-up for runtime: tagging eng-runtime. Proposed changes: - emit `quota_provenance` field in our access logs with values like `api_key:<id>`, `project:<id>`, `ip:<addr>`, `org_default` - surface that in the console for recent requests. This will make incidents like this >5x faster to root-cause.

quota-bot: Incident queued: QNT-4721 (quota-provenance-logging) assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.

derek_prod: Resolution for this thread: customer rotated to project-scoped key + bump applied -> no 429s on follow-up load test. Marking as resolved from ops side. :white_check_mark:
